newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Health of Ceausescu heir still critical - doctors.
newsitem.headline: Health of Ceausescu heir still critical - doctors.

text.p: Nicu Ceausescu, the youngest son of Romania's late Stalinist dictator, was in critical condition in hospital on Tuesday, doctors said.
"His (Nicu's) health condition has remained unchanged. The situation is still serious," Bucharest university hospital spokesman Marius Filip said.
Nicu, 45, was rushed to the hospital late on Sunday with a "serious haemorrhage shock" caused by "varicose oesophagus and a chronic liver cirrhosis", a hospital statement said.
"The bleeding started all of a sudden. Luckily, he was given medical treatment in time," Valentin, his elder brother, told Reuters. "The problem now is to bring the bleeding under control".
Filip said doctors were trying to stop the internal bleeding, which he said was the second after a milder one last month.
Filip said Nicu's present health condition prevented him from undergoing surgery and having a liver transplant.

Nicu, groomed to be Ceausescu's successor, served three years in jail initially over charges linked to ordering the repression of protests in his fiefdom of Sibiu during the December 1989 revolt in which his father and mother were ousted and shot by a firing squad.
The charge was later dropped and only a five-year sentence for illegal gun possession stuck. He was paroled on health grounds in 1992.
